question: What cycle life (number of cycles to 80% capacity) does the review report for the oxyfluoride Li2Mn2/3Nb1/3O2F?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE text ILIKE '%Nb%' OR text ILIKE '%oxyfluoride%' OR text ILIKE '%80%capacity%' OR text ILIKE '%cycle life%' ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, figure_id, fact_no, statement, value, unit FROM figure_facts WHERE statement ILIKE '%Nb%' OR statement ILIKE '%cycle%' OR statement ILIKE '%80%'
SELECT id, page, text FROM sentences WHERE text ILIKE '%DRX%' OR text ILIKE '%disordered rock%' ORDER BY page
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (9,10,11) AND (id LIKE 'p9.L11%' OR id LIKE 'p10.L%' OR id LIKE 'p11.L%') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, figure_id, line_no, text FROM figure_ocr WHERE figure_id='p11.F9' ORDER BY line_no
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE (text ILIKE '%80%' OR text ILIKE '%cycles%' OR text ILIKE '%retention%') ORDER BY page, line_no

rendered: The review gives no cycle-life figure for the DRX oxyfluoride Li2Mn2/3Nb1/3O2F, so it reports no number of cycles to the usual capacity threshold for this material. The only performance value it gives for this material is a specific energy: up to 1000 Wh kg[1], cited to the DRX literature. The accompanying figure for this material is Fig. 9[2]. Its first panel shows charge/discharge curves for only the first few cycles, and its inset plots capacity against cycle number. Neither the text nor the caption states where capacity falls to a fixed fraction of its initial value, so no cycle life can be read as the review's own value.
